business_model.claim: Aeronautical revenue comes from charging departing passenger fees, additional passenger service fees, and aircraft landing and parking fees, which are invoiced principally to airlines.

business_model.claim: Commercial revenue is generated from cargo warehouse usage, duty free shops, retail and food and beverage royalties and space rentals, car parking, fuel, advertising, VIP lounges, and passenger-facing services.

business_model.claim: Under the IFRIC 12 intangible asset model, obligated airport improvements and upgrades are recognized as construction service revenue equal to costs incurred plus a reasonable margin.

quotes: In October 2025, Wizz Airlines launched a new base at Zvartnots Airport, in Armenia, deploying two aircrafts and adding several new European destinations.
In 2025, we also inaugurated a new premium VIP lounge in Ezeiza Airport and a new duty-free arrivals area.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the 2025 20-F Item 4.A history
competitive_position.claim: CAAP expanded its pipeline in late 2025 with concession awards for Baghdad International Airport in Iraq and AIAAN in Angola, though definitive agreements remain under negotiation.
quotes: In November 2025, the consortium formed by the Company and Amwaj International for Real-Estate Investments Co. Ltd. signed an award agreement with the Government of Iraq to operate the Baghdad International Airport.

In December 2025, the consortium formed by the Company, Mota-Engil Engenharia e Construção Africa and BestFly Ltda. was formally notified by the Angolan Ministry of Transport of the award of the public tender for the concession of the right to operate and manage the Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport (“AIAAN”), subject to the execution of the definitive concession agreement and the satisfaction of customary conditions precedent.
On April 7, 2025, the Federal Government of Nigeria discontinued the previous concession allocation processes for four international airports (Lagos, Abuja, Kano, and Port Harcourt).

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the 2025 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Governmental authorities may terminate CAAP concessions for public interest, repeated breach, or re-auction, and since February 2018 the Argentine Government has held the right to buy out the AA2000 concession.
quotes: Termination can occur at any time for public interest reasons or due to our material and repeated breaches of the concession terms.
Pursuant to the AA2000 Concession Agreement, since February 2018, the Argentine Government may buy out our concession, which would materially affect our revenues and operations.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the 2025 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Regulators can alter tariffs, fees, or capital expenditure requirements adversely, including ORSNA in Argentina and authorities reviewing the Florence Airport master plan in Italy.
quotes: The Argentinian National Airports System Regulatory Body (Organismo Regulador del Sistema Nacional de Aeropuertos, “ORSNA”) may adjust the fees we charge for aeronautical services, the payments we are required to make to the Argentine Government and our investment plan in a way that is detrimental to us or fail to adjust them to restore the AA2000 Concession Agreement’s economic equilibrium.

If ORSNA does not approve the capital expenditures already made under the AA2000 Concession Agreement, we could be required to make additional capital expenditures, which may affect our cash flows and financial condition.
The approval process for the Florence Airport master plan requires authorization from both local and national authorities, with informational involvement of the European Commission.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 2025 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors and Q3 2026 interim financial statement Notes 8, 10, and 15
competitive_position.claim: CAAP's Brazilian concession has incurred losses from financial liability accretion on its fixed concession fee and is the only segment with identified impairment indicators in 2025 and 2026.
quotes: We are in a contractual renegotiation process of the Brazilian Concession Agreement under which we incurred losses due to the accretion of the financial liability recognized as a result of the contractual fixed concession fee.
During 2026 and 2025 the Group has not identified impairment indicators except in the Brazilian segment due to the losses from its operations.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the 2025 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors
competitive_position.claim: Armed conflicts and geopolitical escalations—including the Russia-Ukraine war and 2026 Middle East hostilities—threaten passenger flows, airspace access, security costs, and fuel prices across CAAP's network.
quotes: The ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine has and will likely continue to disrupt air travel routes and passenger flows, which could negatively affect our operational performance and results of operations.

Recent geopolitical escalations, including the conflict and related tensions in the Middle East involving Israel and Iran, illustrated the potential for armed conflicts to affect airport infrastructure and operations, including through airport closures, flight cancellations, airspace restrictions or rerouting of air traffic.
As an example, on March 8, 2026, oil prices surged due to the war, reaching U.S.$119.50 a barrel, being that the first time in four years in which prices rose above U.S.$100 per barrel.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the 2025 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors and Q3 2026 interim financial statement Note 15
competitive_position.claim: Meeting concession investment obligations requires substantial capital outlays—such as approximately USD 7.3 billion under the extended AA2000 concession—and failure to execute on budget or on time risks fines or concession termination.
quotes: The total capital investments program, during the term of the extended concession is expected to be approximately USD 7.3 billion (including VAT) to be primarily funded by certain trusts, and of which approximately USD 1.5 billion shall be deployed during the 2027–2031 period across the airports covered by the AA2000 concession.

Failure to fulfill our investment commitments on a timely basis or obtain sufficient financing to fund the projects, could lead to a breach of the relevant concession agreement, potentially resulting in monetary fines or the early termination of our concession agreements.

competitive_position.basis: stated directly in the 2025 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors and Item 5 Macroeconomic Conditions
competitive_position.claim: CAAP faces operating and financial exposure from Argentine hyperinflation, foreign exchange volatility, Uruguay's dependence on Argentine and Brazilian traffic, and growing cybersecurity threats to airport systems.
quotes: Our Uruguayan airport operations, particularly at Punta del Este Airport, are heavily dependent on air traffic from Argentina and Brazil.
The risk of cybercrime has been increasing, especially as infiltrating technology continues to become increasingly sophisticated.

We have determined that, as of July 1, 2018, the Argentine economy qualifies as a hyperinflationary economy therefore according to the guidelines of the IAS 29, our financial statements for periods ending after that date should be adjusted by applying a general price index and expressed in the measuring unit at the end of the reporting period and then such financial information to be translated into the presentation currency at the prevailing exchange rate.

risks.claim: Governments can terminate CAAP's concessions for public interest reasons or breaches, and the Argentine Government can buy out its largest concession in a market where CAAP operates 37 of 56 national airports.
quotes: Our airport concessions may be terminated under various circumstances, many of which are beyond our control.

In the AA2000 Concession Agreement, our largest concession operations, the Argentine Government has the right to buy out the concession agreement upon prior notification to us and indemnify us for certain incurred investments.

Although termination payments vary by concession, they usually include a claim for indemnification equal to the value of our non-amortized investments relating to operating the airports and rendering the services agreed under the concession agreements plus loss of profits.

quotes: We are in a contractual renegotiation process of the Brazilian Concession Agreement under which we incurred losses due to the accretion of the financial liability recognized as a result of the contractual fixed concession fee.

risks.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors, Item 4, and Item 5.
risks.claim: Regulators can detrimentally alter tariffs, government payments, or capital expenditure approvals in Argentina, while permitting delays threaten the Florence Airport master plan in Italy.
quotes: The Argentinian National Airports System Regulatory Body (Organismo Regulador del Sistema Nacional de Aeropuertos, “ORSNA”) may adjust the fees we charge for aeronautical services, the payments we are required to make to the Argentine Government and our investment plan in a way that is detrimental to us or fail to adjust them to restore the AA2000 Concession Agreement’s economic equilibrium.

If ORSNA does not approve the capital expenditures already made under the AA2000 Concession Agreement, we could be required to make additional capital expenditures, which may affect our cash flows and financial condition.
